## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. --- I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode. --- github-actions-visual-workflow-editor.md github-agent-project-comparison.md ios-builder-native-app-generation.md issue-triggered-opencode-workflow.md live-source-file-browser.md omgithub-self-hosted-supabase-migration.md opencode-docker-sandbox.md opencode-oauth-env-auth.md opencode-token-isolation.md remix-preview-port-ownership.md import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs' import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path' import { createHash } from 'node:crypto' import { createServer } from 'node:http' import { spawn } from 'node:child_process' import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url' import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs' import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs' export function projectType(root) { if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) { const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.') if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite' throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.') } if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html' throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.') } export async function start(root = process.cwd()) { const type = projectType(root) const projectRoot = resolve(root) if (type === 'vite') { const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache') mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true }) const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies') const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json') const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex') let old = '' try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {} if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) { await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root }) mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true }) const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex') writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash) } await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root }) root = join(root, 'dist') } if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.') if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) })) const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' } const clients = new Set() const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') }) const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000) const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null const server = createServer((req, res) => { try { const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost') if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') { res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' }) res.write(': connected\n\n') clients.add(res) req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res)) return } const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname)) if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return } const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream') res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache') const content = readFileSync(file) if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') { const html = content.toString() res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}`) : html + livePreviewScript) } else res.end(content) } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') } }) server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() }) server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0') return server } if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D horror game about escaping a terrifying ghost’s house, optimized for phone/tablet, continuing from an earlier failed run.

## Requirements
- 3D game, playable on phone and tablet, responsive touch controls and mobile-safe layout.
- Complete game loop: title, gameplay, win/lose states, restart.
- No clarifying questions; note assumptions when finished.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (≤1280px wide) and read only the latest one; use full-size PNG only for fine detail.
- Existing repo was empty of game code; build from scratch.

## Decisions
- Use a static HTML + vendored Three.js (r170) game with no build step, served by the existing static runtime.
- Theme: “Hollow House” / “귀신의 집에서 탈출하라”; collect 3 black candles to break the sealed foyer door, avoid a ghost.
- Implement ghost AI with roaming/chase/search, hiding wardrobes, sprint stamina, flashlight detection tradeoff, compass to nearest candle/exit, room toasts, subtitles, procedural audio, jumpscare, win/lose screens.
- Merge all static meshes by material for performance (1304 → ~130 draw calls); adaptive resolution added for weak devices.
- Use MeshLambertMaterial broadly instead of MeshStandardMaterial for performance.
- Procedurally generated textures, audio, and jumpscare face (canvas-drawn).
- Added an outdoor sky/path/porch behind the exit door for a satisfying escape view.

## Work State

### Completed
- Created full project structure: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/ghost.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/textures.js`, vendored `vendor/three.module.js`, `vendor/BufferGeometryUtils.js`.
- Implemented title screen, intro overlay, HUD, touch controls, pause, end screens, jumpscare, mobile/desktop responsive CSS.
- Implemented mansion with 9 rooms, colliders, furniture, doors, lighting, fog, dust, paintings, fireplace, chapel, wardrobes, exit door with 3 rune sockets.
- Implemented candle spawning in random distinct rooms, pickup UI, door opening, ghost awaken/final chase, win/lose, restart.
- Verified title/gameplay/candle/pickup/hide/win/end screens via Playwright screenshots.
- Fixed UI overlaps (pause moved right, subtitle/prompt repositioned), candle flame size, fireplace fire, exit wall gap above door, dark outdoor view, adaptive resolution.
- Verified door animation reaches `openness: 1`, rotations `[1.86, -1.86]`.
- Verified win state and stats display, lose state and stats display.
- Reworked jumpscare face into a creepy canvas-drawn face with black hair, red pinprick eyes, jagged teeth.

### Active
- Just fixed a critical movement rotation bug in `movePlayer()` (worldX/worldZ formula); needs browser retest.
- Need final verification of movement/collision, touch layout at mobile sizes, and complete end-to-end playthrough.

### Blocked
- Software-rendered Chromium runs at only ~5 fps even at adaptive 0.58 scale, so screenshots can be slow; use lower viewport (e.g. 960×600) and/or `window.__hollow.setScale(0.5–1)` before capture.

## Next Move
1. Reload and verify W/A/S/D movement and yaw-relative direction after the movement formula fix.
2. Verify collision sliding against walls/furniture and exit crossing; ensure win triggers after door is open.
3. Test mobile landscape (844×390) and portrait (390×844) layouts; ensure pause button, joystick, RUN, LIGHT, USE visible and usable.
4. Test candle pickup → ghost awaken → chase/catch → end screen → Try Again reset.
5. Confirm jumpscare appears for ~2.4s and end screen follows.
6. Capture final polished screenshots (title, gameplay, candle, win) at ≤1280px wide JPEG.
7. Clean up debug leftovers if desired, check console for errors, then summarize assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM structure, all screens/HUD/control markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: responsive UI, HUD, touch controls, jumpscare styles, mobile media queries.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game loop, player, input, interactions, HUD, candle spawning, win/lose/restart, jumpscare drawing, debug API.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: mansion geometry/colliders/dressing, lights, exit door, wardrobes, stove/fireplaces, outdoor scene, static merge support.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ghost.js`: ghost model and AI states/movement/catch.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio ambience, footsteps, heartbeat, whispers, jumpscare.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/textures.js`: canvas textures (wallpaper, wood, stone, rugs, portraits, sky, glow, dust).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/three.module.js`: vendored Three.js r170.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/vendor/BufferGeometryUtils.js`: mergeGeometries import used by main.js.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: latest verification screenshots (`scare3.jpg`, `dooropen3.jpg`, `win.jpg`, `mobile-game.jpg`, etc.).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: existing static server launcher; server currently running on port 3002 in tmux session `hollow`.

## 🕯️ Hollow House — Escape the Ghost

A short first-person 3D horror game built with Three.js. Find all **three black candles** inside the mansion, then escape through the sealed foyer door while a ghost hunts you. Works on phones, tablets, and desktop — no build step.

### Play

```bash
./start.sh
```

Then open the printed local URL. On desktop, click the canvas to capture the mouse; on mobile, use the on-screen joystick and buttons.

### Controls

| Action | Desktop | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `W A S D` / arrow keys | Left joystick |
| Look | Mouse (pointer lock) | Drag on the canvas |
| Sprint | `Shift` | `RUN` button |
| Use / pick up / hide | `E` or `Space` | `USE` |
| Flashlight | `F` | `LIGHT` |
| Pause | `Esc` / pause button | Auto-pauses when the tab is hidden |

### Rules

- Collecting candles wakes the ghost; each one makes it more aggressive.
- Hiding in a wardrobe breaks line of sight, but the ghost can search nearby.
- The flashlight makes the dark manageable — and makes you easier to spot.
- All three candles open the foyer door. Cross the threshold to win.
- Getting caught ends the run; use **Enter Again** to restart.

### Notes / assumptions

- Everything is procedural: geometry, textures, audio, and the jumpscare face. No external assets are fetched at runtime.
- Three.js r170 and `BufferGeometryUtils` are vendored locally, so the game runs offline.
- Static geometry is merged by material at startup to keep the draw-call count low; adaptive resolution drops internal render scale on slow devices.
- The game assumes a WebGL-capable browser with pointer/touch events. Portrait and landscape are both supported.

+| Sprint | `Shift` | `RUN` button |
+| Use / pick up / hide | `E` or `Space` | `USE` |
+| Flashlight | `F` | `LIGHT` |
+| Pause | `Esc` / pause button | Auto-pauses when the tab is hidden |
+
+### Rules
+
+- Collecting candles wakes the ghost; each one makes it more aggressive.
+- Hiding in a wardrobe breaks line of sight, but the ghost can search nearby.
+- The flashlight makes the dark manageable — and makes you easier to spot.
+- All three candles open the foyer door. Cross the threshold to win.
+- Getting caught ends the run; use **Enter Again** to restart.
+
+### Notes / assumptions
+
+- Everything is procedural: geometry, textures, audio, and the jumpscare face. No external assets are fetched at runtime.
+- Three.js r170 and `BufferGeometryUtils` are vendored locally, so the game runs offline.
+- Static geometry is merged by material at startup to keep the draw-call count low; adaptive resolution drops internal render scale on slow devices.
+- The game assumes a WebGL-capable browser with pointer/touch events. Portrait and landscape are both supported.
